Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward read reaches the end of the file without finding any transaction record, indicating the Transaction file is empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the last used Transaction ID to zero, ensuring that when incremented by 1, the first Transaction ID generated will be 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Empty Transaction File - Set Last Used Transaction ID to Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction file contains no existing records (the backward browse reaches the beginning of the file without finding any record), the last used Transaction ID is set to zero so that the first ever Transaction ID will be generated as 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward read of the Transaction file has been completed, either successfully retrieving the last transaction record or determining the file is empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system ends the browse session on the Transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction file browse session is closed and released, making the file available for subsequent write and update operations required to record the new bill payment transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close the Transaction File Browse Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the backward read has been completed (whether a record was found or the file was empty), the Transaction file browse session must be formally closed before any further file operations are performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The last used Transaction ID has been determined — either captured from the last existing transaction record in the file, or set to zero if no transactions exist
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system generates the new Transaction ID for the bill payment transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system increments the last used Transaction ID by exactly 1 to produce the new unique Transaction ID, and this new Transaction ID is set as the identifier for the bill payment transaction record about to be created

all_rules.Rule_Name: Generate New Unique Transaction ID by Incrementing Last Used ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the last used Transaction ID has been determined (either from the last record in the file or zero if the file was empty), the system generates the next unique Transaction ID by adding 1 to the last used value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A confirmed bill payment request has been validated and is ready to be recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins building a new bill payment transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must initialize a completely blank transaction record, clearing all fields to their default empty state before any transaction details are populated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize a Blank Transaction Record Before Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating any bill payment transaction details, a fresh and empty transaction record must be created to ensure no residual or stale data from previous transactions contaminates the new bill payment record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new sequential transaction ID has been generated by adding 1 to the last existing transaction ID found in the transaction file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the new bill payment transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must assign the newly generated unique transaction ID to the Transaction ID field of the transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Unique Transaction ID to Bill Payment Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each bill payment transaction must be assigned a unique, sequentially generated transaction identifier. This ID is derived by retrieving the last existing transaction ID and incrementing it by 1, ensuring no two transactions share the same identifier.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new bill payment transaction record is being built
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the transaction classification fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field must be set to the value '02' to designate this transaction as a bill payment type

all_rules.Rule_Name: Classify Bill Payment with Transaction Type Code '02'
all_rules.Rule_Description: All bill payment transactions must be classified using the standard transaction type code '02', which identifies and distinguishes bill payment transactions from other transaction types within the system.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new bill payment transaction record is being built
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the transaction category
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Category Code field must be set to the numeric value 2 to categorize this transaction as a bill payment category

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Transaction Category Code 2 to Bill Payment
all_rules.Rule_Description: All bill payment transactions must be assigned transaction category code 2, which categorizes the nature of the transaction for reporting, classification, and downstream processing purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new bill payment transaction record is being built
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the transaction origination source
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Source field must be set to 'POS TERM' to indicate the payment was initiated through a Point of Sale Terminal channel

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Transaction Origination Source as POS Terminal
all_rules.Rule_Description: All online bill payment transactions must record their origination source as 'POS TERM' (Point of Sale Terminal), indicating the channel through which the payment was initiated for audit and tracking purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new bill payment transaction record is being built
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the transaction description
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Description field must be set to 'BILL PAYMENT - ONLINE' to provide a clear, standardized description of the bill payment transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Standard Bill Payment Transaction Description
all_rules.Rule_Description: All online bill payment transactions must carry a standardized human-readable description of 'BILL PAYMENT - ONLINE' to clearly identify the nature of the transaction in statements, reports, and transaction histories.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A confirmed bill payment is being processed for an account with a current outstanding balance greater than zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the payment amount on the transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Amount field must be set to the full current account balance, meaning the entire outstanding balance is paid in one transaction with no option for partial payment

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Payment Amount Equal to Full Current Account Balance
all_rules.Rule_Description: A bill payment always pays the entire outstanding account balance in full. The payment amount recorded on the transaction must equal the full current account balance at the time of payment — partial payments are not supported.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account-to-Card cross-reference has been successfully looked up using the Account ID, and the associated card number has been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the card number on the bill payment transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Card Number field must be set to the card number retrieved from the Account-to-Card cross-reference record, linking the payment to the correct card account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Associate Card Number with Bill Payment Transaction
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each bill payment transaction must be linked to the card number associated with the account being paid. The card number is retrieved from the Account-to-Card cross-reference record using the Account ID, ensuring the transaction is traceable to the correct card.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new bill payment transaction record is being built
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the merchant identification details on the transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Merchant ID field must be set to 999999999, the Merchant Name field must be set to 'BILL PAYMENT', the Merchant City field must be set to 'N/A', and the Merchant Zip field must be set to 'N/A', reflecting that bill payments are not associated with a physical merchant location

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Standard Bill Payment Merchant Identification Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: All bill payment transactions must be recorded against a standardized internal merchant profile. The merchant is identified with a fixed Merchant ID of 999999999, Merchant Name of 'BILL PAYMENT', and placeholder values of 'N/A' for both Merchant City and Merchant Zip, as bill payments do not involve a physical merchant location.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A bill payment transaction record is being built and requires timestamp information
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system retrieves the current date and time for timestamping
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must obtain the current date formatted as YYYY-MM-DD and the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS, combine them into a single timestamp value with milliseconds set to zero, making this timestamp available for assignment to the transaction origination and processing time fields

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current Date and Time for Transaction Timestamping
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before recording the transaction timestamps, the system must retrieve the current date and time. The timestamp is formatted as a composite value combining the current date in YYYY-MM-DD format and the current time in HH:MM:SS format, with milliseconds set to zero.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current date and time timestamp has been retrieved and formatted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the origination time on the bill payment transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Origination Timestamp field must be set to the current date and time, recording the exact moment the bill payment transaction was created

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Transaction Origination Timestamp
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each bill payment transaction must record the exact date and time when the transaction was originated. The origination timestamp captures when the payment request was initiated and is set to the current system date and time at the moment of transaction creation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current date and time timestamp has been retrieved and formatted, and the Transaction Origination Timestamp has already been set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the processing time on the bill payment transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Processing Timestamp field must be set to the same current date and time value used for the origination timestamp, indicating that online bill payments are originated and processed at the same point in time

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Transaction Processing Timestamp
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each bill payment transaction must record the exact date and time when the transaction was processed. For online bill payments, the processing timestamp is set to the same current date and time as the origination timestamp, reflecting that the payment is processed immediately upon submission.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A bill payment has been confirmed by the user, a new unique Transaction ID has been generated, and the transaction record has been fully populated with payment details including Transaction Type '02', Category Code 2, Source 'POS TERM', Description 'BILL PAYMENT - ONLINE', the full current account balance as the payment amount, the resolved card number, Merchant ID 999999999, Merchant Name 'BILL PAYMENT', Merchant City 'N/A', Merchant Zip 'N/A', and current timestamps for both origination and processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to write the new bill payment transaction record to the Transaction File using the newly generated Transaction ID as the unique record identifier
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction record is submitted to the Transaction File and the outcome (success, duplicate, or failure) is captured for subsequent processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Submit Bill Payment Transaction Record to Transaction File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user confirms a bill payment, the fully populated bill payment transaction record must be submitted and persisted to the Transaction File using the generated Transaction ID as the unique record key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The bill payment transaction record has been successfully written to the Transaction File without any errors or duplicate key conflicts
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction File confirms the record was written successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays a success message in green color on the Bill Payment screen reading: 'Payment successful. Your Transaction ID is [Transaction ID].' where [Transaction ID] is the actual Transaction ID assigned to the payment, providing the user with a reference number for the completed payment

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Payment Success Confirmation with Transaction ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful writing of the bill payment transaction record to the Transaction File, the system must display a green-colored success confirmation message to the user that includes the assigned Transaction ID for reference.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The bill payment transaction has been successfully written to the Transaction File and the success message has been composed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the Bill Payment screen for display following a successful payment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All input fields on the Bill Payment screen are cleared: the Account ID field is set to blank, the Current Balance display field is set to blank, the Confirmation field is set to blank, and the message area is cleared — leaving the screen ready for a fresh bill payment entry, with the cursor positioned on the Account ID field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Input Fields After Successful Payment
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a bill payment is successfully processed and the success message is prepared, all input fields on the Bill Payment screen must be cleared to allow the user to initiate a new bill payment transaction if needed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A bill payment transaction record has been submitted to the Transaction File with a generated Transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction File detects that the Transaction ID already exists — either as a duplicate key or a duplicate record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The bill payment is rejected, an error flag is set, the error message 'Tran ID already exist...' is displayed on the Bill Payment screen, the cursor is positioned on the Account ID field, and the user is returned to the Bill Payment screen to review the situation — no transaction is recorded and no account balance update occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Bill Payment Transaction with Duplicate Transaction ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the generated Transaction ID already exists in the Transaction File (duplicate key or duplicate record condition), the bill payment must be rejected and the user must be notified that the transaction could not be recorded due to a duplicate Transaction ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A bill payment transaction record has been submitted to the Transaction File with a generated Transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction File write operation fails for any reason other than a duplicate key or duplicate record condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The bill payment is rejected, an error flag is set, the error message 'Unable to Add Bill pay Transaction...' is displayed on the Bill Payment screen, the cursor is positioned on the Account ID field, and the user is returned to the Bill Payment screen — no transaction is recorded and no account balance update occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Unexpected Transaction File Write Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Transaction File write operation fails for any reason other than a duplicate Transaction ID, the bill payment must be rejected and the user must be informed that the bill payment transaction could not be added.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A bill payment transaction has been confirmed by the user with 'Y', the transaction record has been successfully written to the transaction file, and the current account balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL) and the transaction amount (TRAN-AMT) are both set to the full outstanding balance amount
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system computes the new account balance by subtracting the transaction payment amount (TRAN-AMT) from the current account balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account's current balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL) is updated to the result of Current Balance minus Payment Amount, which equals zero, reflecting that the full outstanding balance has been paid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compute New Account Balance After Bill Payment
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a confirmed bill payment transaction has been successfully recorded, the system calculates the new account balance by subtracting the full payment amount (which equals the entire current balance) from the current account balance, resulting in a zero balance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account's current balance has been recalculated to zero after subtracting the payment amount, and the account record (ACCOUNT-RECORD) in memory reflects the updated balance
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system rewrites the updated account record to the Account Data File (ACCTDAT) using the account record that was previously locked for update during the account read operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Data File (ACCTDAT) is updated with the new account record containing the zero balance, and the system evaluates whether the update was successful, resulted in an account not found condition, or encountered another failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Updated Account Balance to Account Data File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the new zero account balance has been computed, the system persists the updated account record back to the Account Data File (ACCTDAT) by rewriting the full account record with the new balance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to rewrite the updated account record to the Account Data File (ACCTDAT) after computing the new zero balance
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Data File returns a 'Not Found' response, meaning the account record no longer exists in the file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Account ID NOT found...' on the Bill Payment screen, positions the cursor on the Account ID input field, and redisplays the Bill Payment screen to allow the user to correct the Account ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Not Found Error During Balance Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the account record cannot be located in the Account Data File during the balance update rewrite operation, the system raises a business error indicating the account does not exist and prompts the user to re-enter the Account ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to rewrite the updated account record to the Account Data File (ACCTDAT) after computing the new zero balance
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Data File returns any failure response other than 'Not Found' (i.e., an unexpected system or file error occurs during the update)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Unable to Update Account...' on the Bill Payment screen, positions the cursor on the Account ID input field, and redisplays the Bill Payment screen to allow the user to take corrective action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Update Failure Error During Balance Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the account record update to the Account Data File fails for any reason other than account not found (e.g., file unavailable or system error), the system raises a business error indicating the account could not be updated and prompts the user to re-enter the Account ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The bill payment transaction record has been successfully written to the transaction file AND the account balance has been successfully updated to zero in the Account Data File (ACCTDAT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Data File confirms a successful rewrite of the updated account record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears all input fields on the Bill Payment screen (Account ID, Current Balance, Confirmation field, and message area), displays the success message 'Payment successful. Your Transaction ID is [Transaction ID].' in green color on the Bill Payment screen, where [Transaction ID] is the newly generated transaction reference number assigned to this payment

all_rules.Rule_Name: Payment Success Notification After Successful Account Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the account balance has been successfully updated to zero in the Account Data File, the system notifies the user that the bill payment was completed successfully and provides the generated Transaction ID as a payment reference. All input fields are cleared to reset the screen for a new transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A bill payment transaction has been successfully written to the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the successful payment completion
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID input field is cleared to spaces, the Current Balance display field is cleared to spaces, the Confirmation input field is cleared to spaces, and the message area is cleared to spaces, so that all input fields are reset and ready for a new bill payment entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Input Fields After Successful Bill Payment
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful recording of a bill payment transaction, all input fields on the Bill Payment screen — Account ID, Current Balance, Confirmation Field, and any existing messages — must be cleared to prepare the screen for a fresh entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A bill payment transaction has been successfully written to the Transaction File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the success notification for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error/message field color attribute on the Bill Payment screen is set to green (DFHGREEN), ensuring the success message is visually differentiated from error messages which appear in the default color

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Success Message Display Color to Green
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a bill payment is successfully processed and the transaction is recorded, the message displayed to the user must appear in green color to visually distinguish a successful outcome from error messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A bill payment transaction has been successfully written to the Transaction File and a Transaction ID has been assigned to the payment record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system builds the success notification message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message is constructed by concatenating: 'Payment successful. ' + 'Your Transaction ID is ' + the assigned Transaction ID value (trimmed of trailing spaces) + '.', and this complete message string is stored in the message field to be displayed on the Bill Payment screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build Payment Success Message with Assigned Transaction ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful bill payment, the system must construct and display a confirmation message that includes the phrase 'Payment successful.' followed by the unique Transaction ID assigned to the payment, so the user has a reference number for the completed transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The success message has been built with the Transaction ID, the message color has been set to green, all input fields have been cleared, and the screen header information (current date, current time, transaction name, program name) has been populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Bill Payment screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Bill Payment screen (map COBIL0A from mapset COBIL00) is displayed with the green success message 'Payment successful. Your Transaction ID is [ID].', all input fields (Account ID, Current Balance, Confirmation) are blank, the screen header shows the current date and time, and the cursor is positioned at the Account ID field — indicating the screen is ready for the next bill payment entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Bill Payment Screen with Green Success Message and Cleared Input Fields
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful bill payment, the Bill Payment screen must be refreshed and sent to the user showing the green success message with the Transaction ID, all input fields cleared, and the screen header updated with the current date and time — signaling the system is ready to accept the next bill payment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Bill Payment screen with an active session and has previously entered data in any of the input fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF4 function key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system triggers the Screen Clear and Reset process, clearing all input fields and redisplaying a blank Bill Payment screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Screen Clear on PF4 Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the PF4 function key on the Bill Payment screen, the system initiates a full screen clear and reset sequence.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Bill Payment screen and has entered a valid Account ID along with 'N' or 'n' in the Confirmation field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the ENTER key with 'N' or 'n' in the Confirmation field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system treats the entry as a cancellation, triggers the Screen Clear and Reset process, sets the error flag ON, and redisplays a blank Bill Payment screen without processing any payment

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Screen Clear on Payment Cancellation via N
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters 'N' or 'n' in the Confirmation field, the system treats this as a cancellation and initiates a full screen clear and reset, discarding any entered data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen clear and reset process has been triggered either by PF4 key press or by the user entering 'N'/'n' in the Confirmation field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID input field is set to blank (spaces), removing any previously entered account number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Account ID Field on Screen Reset
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the screen clear and reset process, the Account ID input field is cleared to blank so the user can enter a new account number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen clear and reset process has been triggered either by PF4 key press or by the user entering 'N'/'n' in the Confirmation field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Balance display field is set to blank (spaces), removing any previously displayed account balance

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Current Balance Display Field on Screen Reset
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the screen clear and reset process, the Current Balance display field is cleared to blank so no previously retrieved balance information remains visible.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen clear and reset process has been triggered either by PF4 key press or by the user entering 'N'/'n' in the Confirmation field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Confirmation input field is set to blank (spaces), removing any previously entered Y or N confirmation value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Confirmation Field on Screen Reset
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the screen clear and reset process, the Confirmation input field is cleared to blank so any previously entered confirmation response (Y/N) is removed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen clear and reset process has been triggered either by PF4 key press or by the user entering 'N'/'n' in the Confirmation field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The working storage message field (WS-MESSAGE) is set to blank (spaces), removing any previously displayed error or informational messages from the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Messages on Screen Reset
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the screen clear and reset process, all informational and error messages displayed on the Bill Payment screen are cleared to blank.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen clear and reset process has been triggered either by PF4 key press or by the user entering 'N'/'n' in the Confirmation field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the field initialization routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor length indicator for the Account ID field (ACTIDINL) is set to -1, which positions the cursor on the Account ID input field when the screen is redisplayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Cursor Position to Account ID Field on Screen Reset
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the screen clear and reset process, the cursor is repositioned to the Account ID input field so the user can immediately begin entering a new account number without manually navigating to the field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All input fields (Account ID, Current Balance, Confirmation) and all messages have been cleared as part of the screen reset process
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Bill Payment screen back to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Bill Payment screen is redisplayed with all input fields blank, no error or informational messages, and the screen header populated with the current date (MM-DD-YY format), current time (HH:MM:SS format), transaction name, and program name; the cursor is positioned on the Account ID field awaiting new input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay Blank Bill Payment Screen with Refreshed Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all fields and messages have been cleared, the system redisplays the Bill Payment screen in a blank state with an updated header showing current date, time, transaction name, and program name, ready for new user input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Bill Payment screen is about to be displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen header information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time using the built-in CURRENT-DATE function and stores it in the working date/time data area (WS-CURDATE-DATA) for subsequent formatting and display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the Bill Payment screen, the system retrieves the current system date and time to ensure the screen header reflects accurate, real-time information for the user session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Bill Payment screen header is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the application title fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) is placed into the screen header Title Line 1 field (TITLE01O), and Application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) is placed into the screen header Title Line 2 field (TITLE02O)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Application Title Lines in Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Bill Payment screen header must display two lines of the application title sourced from the centrally maintained application title definitions (CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02), ensuring consistent branding across all screens.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Bill Payment screen header is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the transaction identifier field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is placed into the screen header Transaction Name field (TRNNAMEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Transaction ID in Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Bill Payment screen header must display the current transaction identifier (WS-TRANID) so the user and support staff can identify the active transaction context during the bill payment session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Bill Payment screen header is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the program name field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is placed into the screen header Program Name field (PGMNAMEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Program Name in Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Bill Payment screen header must display the name of the currently executing program (WS-PGMNAME) to provide context identification on the screen, supporting navigation awareness and auditability.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date has been retrieved and stored in WS-CURDATE-DATA
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the date for screen header display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The month component (WS-CURDATE-MONTH) is moved to WS-CURDATE-MM, the day component (WS-CURDATE-DAY) is moved to WS-CURDATE-DD, the last two digits of the year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR positions 3 and 4) are moved to WS-CURDATE-YY, and the assembled MM-DD-YY formatted date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) is placed into the screen header Current Date field (CURDATEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Date as MM-DD-YY in Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current date displayed in the Bill Payment screen header must be formatted in MM-DD-YY format. The month, day, and two-digit year are extracted from the retrieved system date and assembled into the standard display format before being placed in the screen header date field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system time has been retrieved and stored in WS-CURDATE-DATA
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the time for screen header display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The hours component (WS-CURTIME-HOURS) is moved to WS-CURTIME-HH, the minutes component (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE) is moved to WS-CURTIME-MM, the seconds component (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) is moved to WS-CURTIME-SS, and the assembled HH:MM:SS formatted time (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) is placed into the screen header Current Time field (CURTIMEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Time as HH:MM:SS in Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current time displayed in the Bill Payment screen header must be formatted in HH:MM:SS format. The hours, minutes, and seconds are extracted from the retrieved system time and assembled into the standard display format before being placed in the screen header time field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A business message may have been set in WS-MESSAGE during the current processing cycle (e.g., validation error, confirmation prompt, or success notification)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the Bill Payment screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The content of WS-MESSAGE is moved to the screen output message field (ERRMSGO of COBIL0AO), making it visible to the user on the rendered screen; if WS-MESSAGE is spaces, the message area on screen will be blank

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Pending Business Message in Screen Message Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: Any business message that has been set during processing (such as validation errors, confirmation prompts, or success notifications) must be transferred to the screen's message display area (ERRMSGO) so the user receives relevant feedback when the screen is rendered.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All screen fields including application titles, transaction ID, program name, current date, current time, account balance, and any business messages have been populated in the screen output area (COBIL0AO)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Bill Payment screen to the user's terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Bill Payment screen (map COBIL0A, mapset COBIL00) is rendered from the populated output data (COBIL0AO), the terminal display is fully erased and replaced with the new screen content, and the cursor is positioned at the designated input field to guide user interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Render and Send Bill Payment Screen to User
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all header, data, and message fields have been populated, the fully assembled Bill Payment screen (map COBIL0A from mapset COBIL00) is sent to the user's terminal, erasing any previous screen content and positioning the cursor at the designated input field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Return to Previous Screen process has been initiated and the destination program field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) in the communication area contains spaces or low-values (i.e., no previous screen has been defined)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the destination program field before transferring control
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On Screen (COSGN00C) as the default navigation target

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Navigation Destination When No Previous Screen Is Defined
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system initiates a return to a previous screen but no destination program has been set in the communication area, the system defaults the navigation target to the Sign-On Screen (COSGN00C) to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF3 on the Bill Payment screen and the system is determining where to navigate back to
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the originating program field (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM contains spaces or low-values (no originating program recorded), the destination is set to the main menu screen (COMEN01C); otherwise, the destination is set to the originating program stored in CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Navigation Destination Based on Originating Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 to navigate back, the system determines the correct destination by checking whether an originating program is recorded in the communication area. If one exists, the user is returned to that program; otherwise, the user is directed to the main menu.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Return to Previous Screen process has been initiated and the destination program has been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the communication area before transferring control
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system updates the communication area by: (1) copying the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) into the originating transaction ID field (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), (2) copying the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) into the originating program field (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), and (3) setting the program context indicator (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) to zeros

all_rules.Rule_Name: Update Communication Area with Current Program Context Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to another screen, the system records the current Bill Payment program's identity (program name and transaction ID) into the communication area, and resets the program context indicator to zero. This ensures the receiving screen knows which program initiated the navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The communication area has been updated with the current program name, transaction ID, and context, and the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) has been set to either the originating program, the main menu (COMEN01C), or the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the screen transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the destination program identified in CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, and the full communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is passed to the receiving program so that session context is preserved across the navigation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Destination Screen with Communication Area

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A bill payment has been confirmed by the user with a valid Account ID and a positive current balance
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is about to open the transaction file to find the last used Transaction ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Highest Possible Starting Position for Transaction File Backward Browse
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before opening the transaction file for backward browsing, the system must set the starting search position to the absolute highest possible Transaction ID value so that the backward read will retrieve the most recently created (last) transaction record in the file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction ID search key has been set to the highest possible value (HIGH-VALUES) and a confirmed bill payment is being processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system requests to open the transaction file for backward browsing using the highest Transaction ID as the starting position
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction file is opened for backward browsing starting from the highest Transaction ID position, and the system is ready to read the previous (most recent) transaction record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Transaction File for Backward Browsing to Retrieve Last Transaction ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must open the transaction file in backward-browse mode, starting from the highest Transaction ID position, in order to locate the most recently created transaction and derive the next sequential Transaction ID for the new bill payment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has requested to open the transaction file for backward browsing starting from the highest Transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction file opens successfully without any errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system confirms the file is open and ready, and proceeds to read the previous transaction record to retrieve the last used Transaction ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Transaction File Open Allows Proceeding to Read Last Transaction
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the transaction file is successfully opened for backward browsing, the system confirms readiness and proceeds to read the previous transaction record to determine the last used Transaction ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has requested to open the transaction file for backward browsing starting from the highest Transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction file open fails because no transactions are found (Transaction ID NOT found condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to 'Y', (2) display the error message 'Transaction ID NOT found...' on the Bill Payment screen, (3) place the cursor focus on the Account ID field, and (4) redisplay the Bill Payment screen — stopping all further bill payment processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Block Bill Payment When No Transactions Exist in Transaction File
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the transaction file cannot be opened for backward browsing because no transactions are found (file is empty or no matching record exists at the starting position), the system must stop the bill payment process and notify the user with an appropriate error message, directing their attention back to the Account ID field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has requested to open the transaction file for backward browsing starting from the highest Transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction file open fails due to any reason other than a not-found condition (i.e., an unexpected system or file access failure)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to 'Y', (2) display the error message 'Unable to lookup Transaction...' on the Bill Payment screen, (3) place the cursor focus on the Account ID field, and (4) redisplay the Bill Payment screen — stopping all further bill payment processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Block Bill Payment on Unexpected Transaction File Access Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the transaction file cannot be opened for backward browsing due to any unexpected failure other than a not-found condition, the system must stop the bill payment process and notify the user with an appropriate error message, directing their attention back to the Account ID field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A bill payment confirmation has been received and the system needs to generate the next sequential Transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates a backward browse of the Transaction file starting from the highest possible Transaction ID (HIGH-VALUES) and reads the previous record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The last existing Transaction record is retrieved, making the most recent Transaction ID available so that the next sequential Transaction ID can be generated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Browse Transaction File Backwards from Highest Transaction ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: To retrieve the most recently created transaction, the system initiates a backward browse of the Transaction file starting from the highest possible Transaction ID value, then reads the previous record to obtain the last existing transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has initiated a backward browse of the Transaction file from the highest Transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward read operation completes successfully and a Transaction record is found
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID from the retrieved record is stored as the last known Transaction ID, and the system proceeds to generate the next Transaction ID by incrementing this value by 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Retrieval of Last Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the backward browse successfully retrieves the last transaction record, the Transaction ID from that record is captured and used as the basis for generating the next sequential Transaction ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is performing a backward browse of the Transaction file to find the last Transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward read operation reaches the end of the file without finding any records, indicating the Transaction file is empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID is defaulted to zero, so that when incremented by 1, the first bill payment transaction will be assigned Transaction ID 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Transaction ID to Zero When Transaction File is Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction file contains no existing records (empty file condition), the system defaults the last Transaction ID to zero, ensuring the first transaction ever created will be assigned Transaction ID 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is performing a backward browse of the Transaction file to retrieve the last Transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward read operation fails for a reason other than the file being empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The bill payment process is stopped, an error flag is set, the error message 'Unable to lookup Transaction...' is displayed to the user on the Bill Payment screen, and the cursor is positioned on the Account ID field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Transaction File Read Failure During ID Generation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the backward browse of the Transaction file fails for any reason other than an empty file, the system halts the bill payment process and notifies the user that the transaction lookup was unsuccessful.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The last Transaction ID has been determined — either retrieved from the last existing transaction record or defaulted to zero because the Transaction file is empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction file browse is ended and the system prepares to create a new bill payment transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The new Transaction ID is computed as the last Transaction ID plus 1, ensuring each transaction receives a unique, sequentially incremented identifier

all_rules.Rule_Name: Generate Next Sequential Transaction ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the last Transaction ID is determined (either from the last existing record or defaulted to zero for an empty file), the system generates the next Transaction ID by incrementing the last known Transaction ID by exactly 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A backward browse of the Transaction file has been initiated to retrieve the last Transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward read operation has completed — whether a record was found, the file was empty, or an error occurred
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The browse session on the Transaction file is formally ended, releasing the browse cursor, and the system proceeds to use the retrieved or defaulted Transaction ID for next-ID generation

all_rules.Rule_Name: End Transaction File Browse After Last Record Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the backward browse operation to retrieve the last Transaction ID is complete (regardless of outcome), the system must formally close the browse session on the Transaction file before proceeding with any further processing.

description:
COBIL00C is a CICS online bill payment program within the CardDemo application that allows users to pay their credit card account balance in full. The program reads the account details, retrieves the associated card cross-reference, generates a new transaction record for the bill payment, updates the account balance to zero, and presents the user with a confirmation screen showing the transaction ID upon successful payment.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: VSAM/CICS Files (ACCTDAT, CXACAIX, TRANSACT) - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Session Initialization - When the program is first invoked (no communication area), redirect the user to the sign-on screen, ensuring only authenticated users can access the bill payment function. 2: Screen Entry Setup - On first entry into the bill payment screen, initialize the display fields, pre-populate the Account ID if one was passed from a previous screen, and display the bill payment screen to the user. 3: User Input Reception - Receive and capture the data entered by the user on the bill payment screen, including Account ID and payment confirmation indicator. 4: Navigation Key Handling - Process function key presses: PF3 returns the user to the previous screen (or main menu if no prior screen), PF4 clears the current screen, and any other invalid key displays an error message. 5: Account ID Validation - Validate that the Account ID field is not blank or empty before proceeding; display an error message prompting the user to enter an Account ID if it is missing. 6: Payment Confirmation Input Handling - Evaluate the confirmation field entered by the user: accept 'Y' or 'y' to proceed with payment, accept 'N' or 'n' to cancel and clear the screen, treat blank as a request to look up the account without confirming, and reject any other value with an error message. 7: Account Balance Lookup - Retrieve the current account balance and account details from the account data file using the provided Account ID, displaying an error if the account is not found. 8: Zero Balance Check - After retrieving the account, verify that the current balance is greater than zero; if the balance is zero or negative, inform the user there is nothing to pay and prevent further processing. 9: Display Current Balance - Display the current account balance on the bill payment screen so the user can review the amount due before confirming payment. 10: Prompt for Payment Confirmation - When the account is found and has a balance but the user has not yet confirmed, prompt the user to confirm the bill payment by displaying a confirmation message. 11: Card Cross-Reference Lookup - When the user confirms payment, retrieve the card number associated with the account from the card cross-reference file using the Account ID. 12: New Transaction ID Generation - Determine the next available transaction ID by browsing the transaction file from the highest existing transaction ID backwards to find the last used ID, then increment it by one to generate a unique new transaction ID. 13: Bill Payment Transaction Record Creation - Build a new transaction record with all required details: the new transaction ID, transaction type code '02', category code 2, source 'POS TERM', description 'BILL PAYMENT - ONLINE', the full current account balance as the payment amount, the associated card number, merchant ID 999999999, merchant name 'BILL PAYMENT', and current timestamp for both origination and processing times. 14: Transaction Record Write - Write the newly created bill payment transaction record to the transaction file, ensuring no duplicate transaction IDs exist. 15: Account Balance Update - After successfully recording the transaction, subtract the payment amount from the account's current balance (resulting in zero balance) and update the account record in the account data file. 16: Payment Success Notification - Upon successful completion of the bill payment, display a success message to the user in green text showing the transaction ID assigned to the payment, and clear all input fields for a fresh entry. 17: Screen Clear / Reset - Clear all input and display fields on the bill payment screen (Account ID, current balance, confirmation field, and messages) and redisplay a blank bill payment screen. 18: Bill Payment Screen Display - Populate the screen header with application title, program name, transaction ID, current date, and current time, then render the bill payment screen with any relevant messages or data. 19: Return to Previous Screen - Transfer control back to the calling program or the main menu, passing along the communication area with updated program context information.
